angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 533,602 km at 38.63 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 25.8847 +/- 0.0128 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 38.63 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.767 +/- 0.024 solar radii from Desidera et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 18599 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A.158D/abstract): 533,602 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.863 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Desidera et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 18599 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A.158D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5145 +/- 50 K from Desidera et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 18599 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A.158D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Desidera et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 18599 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A.158D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-18599.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.604, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
